dispute_ticket.description: I did not vomit or spill anything. I was charged S$180 and I ask for a full refund. I was perfectly fine the whole trip.

chat_logs.content: I am at Pickup Point B, white Alphard.

app_events.details: Rider R-5532 booked trip RYDE-PS-004 from Changi Airport T3 to Blk 233 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3.
Driver submitted cleaning claim S$180.00 with 1 photo and a cleaning receipt.
Receipt attached: QuickValet Car Care, Kaki Bukit Ave 3, S$180.00, dated 2026-10-09 09:00.
S$180.00 cleaning fee charged to rider payment method (credit card).

cleaning_fee_max.text: The maximum cleaning fee in SGD that may be charged to a rider for one trip. The fee is paid to the driver.

cleaning_fee_tiers.value: food or drink spill up to S$40; stains (mud, dirt) and bodily fluids up to S$120; vomit up to S$200
cleaning_fee_tiers.text: Usual fee by type of mess; a fee above the tier for the mess type needs a receipt.

cleaning_claim_evidence_required.value: photo of the mess and a cleaning receipt where available
cleaning_claim_evidence_required.text: Evidence a driver must provide to support a cleaning fee claim against a rider. It governs driver cleaning claims only.

photo_window_after_dropoff_min.text: A cleaning claim needs at least one photo of the mess taken within 60 minutes after drop-off, at or near the drop-off point.

photo_doubt_rule.text: If a photo's authenticity, timing, place or content is in doubt, a case officer decides; the fee is neither confirmed nor removed automatically.

rider_may_dispute_if.text: Lists the grounds on which a rider may dispute a cleaning fee charged to them.

evidence.description: Vomit on the rear seat after the passenger got off at Ang Mo Kio.

expected_outcome.reason: The photo is stamped 23:06 (18 min after the 22:48 drop-off) at GPS about 80 m from the drop-off, and a receipt for S$180 (within the S$200 vomit cap) is attached, so the metadata and paperwork look in order. But the image itself shows an empty grey seat with no vomit or stain and carries a 'pollinations.ai' watermark, i.e. it is an AI-generated image, not a photo of the mess described in the caption. The rider denies any mess. Its authenticity and content are in doubt, so under this trip's photo-doubt rule a case officer decides; the fee is neither confirmed nor removed automatically.
